title: Canonical compactification projection: normalization, inverse and restriction
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{q}Y)$ with $j$ open, $q$ proper and $f=qj$, with $Z$ also separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Put $\Lambda=\mathrm{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)$, the finite-subextension-valued condensed algebraic closure [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and $\mathcal C_T=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(T,\Lambda)$ with exactly the bounded-constructible internal-module predicate of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Use the restricted functors and relative derived tensors of [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors], $F_c=Rq_*j_!$ of [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek], and the specified composition isomorphism $a:Lj^*Lq^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*$ of [def-sfb-dc-upper-star-comp]. The restricted adjunctions and all tensor maps below are the restrictions of the actual ambient module-object structures.
For $K\in\mathcal C_X$ and $B\in\mathcal C_Y$, put $A=j_!K$. Let $\alpha_{A,B}:Rq_*A\otimes B\to Rq_*(A\otimes Lq^*B)$ be the adjoint under $Lq^*\dashv Rq_*$ of the actual oplax map $\delta_q$ followed by $\varepsilon_A\otimes1$, where $\varepsilon$ is this adjunction's counit. Let $\eta,\varepsilon^j$ be the unit and counit of $j_!\dashv Lj^*$ [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-adjunction], and let $\mu_j$ be the actual lax pullback tensor map, inverse to $\delta_j$. For $N\in\mathcal C_Z$ define
$$Q_{K,N}=\varepsilon^j_{j_!K\otimes N}\circ j_!(\mu_{j,j_!K,N})\circ j_!(\eta_K\otimes1):j_!(K\otimes Lj^*N)\longrightarrow j_!K\otimes N.$$
Under the specified section-module equivalences $D(E_T)$ of [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison], $\alpha$ is the canonical ringed-topos projection arrow of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], and $Q$ is the ringed open projection with precisely these unit, lax tensor and counit maps. Both $\alpha_{A,B}$ and $Q_{K,N}$ are invertible. Define
$$P^c_{K,B}=Rq_*j_!(1_K\otimes a_B)\circ Rq_*(Q_{K,Lq^*B}^{-1})\circ\alpha_{A,B}:F_cK\otimes B\longrightarrow F_c(K\otimes Lf^*B).$$
This specified composite is invertible in $\mathcal C_Y$, with two-sided inverse
$$R^c_{K,B}=\alpha_{A,B}^{-1}\circ Rq_*(Q_{K,Lq^*B})\circ Rq_*j_!(1_K\otimes a_B^{-1}).$$
In particular $R^c_{K,B}P^c_{K,B}=1$ and $P^c_{K,B}R^c_{K,B}=1$. For every $h:B\to B'$ in $\mathcal C_Y$ it satisfies
$$P^c_{K,B'}\circ(1_{F_cK}\otimes h)=F_c(1_K\otimes Lf^*h)\circ P^c_{K,B}.$$
At the chosen compactification $c_f$ this is exactly the component of the target's $\mathrm{boundedConstructibleExceptionalProjection}$, including its ambient inclusion and composition comparison. No identification with a common finite coefficient-stage category is part of this assertion.

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors], the tensors, functors and adjunctions here are restrictions along full inclusions. Apply [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] to $q$ and $j$: it identifies the actual oplax map and proper counit, hence their adjoint $\alpha$, with the specified ringed projection mate; for $j$ it identifies extension by zero, its unit, counit and actual lax map. Applying these identifications to the three factors defining $Q$ gives exactly the ringed open projection composite. This verifies equality of the specified arrows, rather than merely identifying their endpoints.

proof.text: The coefficient $\Lambda$ is the algebraic-closure case of [lem-pd-condensed-proper-projection-formula]. Apply that statement to $f=qj$, its given compactification and $K,B$: its $A=Di_!K$ is our $j_!K$, and its adjoint-defined arrow is exactly $\alpha_{A,B}$, so $\alpha$ is invertible. Apply [lem-pd-condensed-open-exceptional-projection-formula] with $U=X$, ambient scheme $Z$, and arbitrary $N\in\mathcal C_Z$. Its displayed $q_{j,K,N}$ is term for term our $Q_{K,N}$, and it is an isomorphism in the restricted category. All schemes remain separated finite type over $k$, as required.

proof.text: Set $s_B=Rq_*j_!(1_K\otimes a_B)$ and $t_B=Rq_*(Q_{K,Lq^*B})$. The specified natural comparison [def-sfb-dc-upper-star-comp] makes $s_B$ invertible, with inverse $Rq_*j_!(1_K\otimes a_B^{-1})$. Functoriality gives $t_B^{-1}=Rq_*(Q_{K,Lq^*B}^{-1})$. Thus $P_B=s_Bt_B^{-1}\alpha_B$ and the claimed $R_B=\alpha_B^{-1}t_Bs_B^{-1}$. Associativity and cancellation give $R_BP_B=\alpha_B^{-1}t_Bt_B^{-1}\alpha_B=1$ and $P_BR_B=s_Bt_B^{-1}t_Bs_B^{-1}=1$. These equations hold inside the full subcategory because its morphisms and composition are inherited.

proof.text: For $h:B\to B'$, write $u=1_{F_cK}\otimes h$, $v=Rq_*(1_A\otimes Lq^*h)$, $w=Rq_*j_!(1_K\otimes Lj^*Lq^*h)$ and $z=F_c(1_K\otimes Lf^*h)$. Naturality of the ringed mate [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], identified in Step 1, says $\alpha_{B'}u=v\alpha_B$. Naturality of the precise open comparison [lem-pd-condensed-open-exceptional-projection-formula] says $t_{B'}w=vt_B$; multiplying by the inverses gives $t_{B'}^{-1}v=wt_B^{-1}$. Naturality of $a$ [def-sfb-dc-upper-star-comp] says $s_{B'}w=zs_B$. Substitution yields $P_{B'}u=s_{B'}t_{B'}^{-1}v\alpha_B=s_{B'}wt_B^{-1}\alpha_B=zP_B$, the required equation.

proof.text: At $c=c_f$, [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek] defines $F_c$ to be the chosen lower shriek, with its ambient inclusion. Unfold the upstream definitions in WeilConjectures/PoincareDuality/ProjectionFormula.lean: exceptionalProjectionMorphismOfCompactification (lines 602–611) is $\alpha$ followed by $Rq_*(Q^{-1}\circ j_!(1\otimes a))$; the inverse component of leftDerivedUpperStarCompactificationIso is exactly $a$. Functoriality separates its last two factors to give $P^{c_f}$. boundedConstructibleExceptionalProjectionMorphism (lines 674–680) wraps that same ambient morphism with ObjectProperty.homMk, and boundedConstructibleExceptionalProjection (lines 750–759) uses precisely those components. Faithfulness of the full inclusion therefore gives the asserted component equality, including the composition comparison; no coefficient-stage identification enters this calculation.
